## About

The **PRC Data Challenges** invite data scientists, researchers, and aviation enthusiasts to tackle real-world aviation performance questions using open data. Organised by the [Performance Review Commission (PRC)](https://ansperformance.eu/about/prc/) of EUROCONTROL in collaboration with the [OpenSky Network](https://opensky-network.org/), each challenge defines a specific prediction or estimation task, provides curated open datasets, and evaluates submissions on a public leaderboard.

A core objective of the PRC Data Challenges is to foster **transparency and reproducibility** in aviation analytics. All participating teams are required to publish their code in open Git repositories, making their methodologies fully inspectable and reproducible. This approach aligns with the PRC's broader mission to democratise access to performance data and analytical methods, enabling independent validation and building a shared body of open, peer-reviewed techniques for the aviation community.

Each edition ranks the submissions by their root mean square error (RMSE) on a test set of flights whose true values the participants do not see. The RMSE is the square root of the average squared difference between the predicted and the true values; it is in the unit of the quantity predicted, and lower is better. The top three teams share a prize of 5,000 EUR.

For more information, visit the [PRC Data Challenge programme page](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/).


## Challenge Editions

:::: {.challenge-card}

### 2026 PRC Data Challenge — Taxi-Out Time Prediction

Participants predicted the taxi-out time of departing flights at ten major European airports: the time, in seconds, from when an aircraft leaves its parking stand (off-block) to when it takes off. The airports were Frankfurt (EDDF), Munich (EDDM), London Heathrow (EGLL), Amsterdam Schiphol (EHAM), Barcelona (LEBL), Madrid (LEMD), Paris Charles de Gaulle (LFPG), Rome Fiumicino (LIRF), Istanbul (LTFM) and Zurich (LSZH). The challenge ran from 1 September to 14 October 2026.

The dataset holds 4,167,797 airport movements, matched to the flight list of the EUROCONTROL Network Manager (the service that processes flight plans for European airspace). Unlike the two earlier editions, it contains no ADS-B trajectories (the positions that aircraft broadcast and the OpenSky Network collects).

**Winners** (ranked by RMSE in seconds, presented at the [14th OpenSky Symposium](https://symposium.opensky-network.org/), Madrid, 29-30 October 2026):

| Place | Team | RMSE | Members | Affiliation | Country | Code |
|-------|------|-----:|---------|-------------|:-------:|:----:|
| 1st | [charming-eel](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/dc2026/winners.html) | 176.16 s | A. Chawla | — | US | — |
| 2nd | [zesty-puzzle](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/dc2026/winners.html) | 180.18 s | L. Melzer | Leibniz Universität Hannover | DE | — |
| 3rd | [youthful-giraffe](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/dc2026/winners.html) | 183.66 s | M. Motoki | — | ID | — |

### 2025 PRC Data Challenge — Fuel Burn Estimation

Participants estimated the fuel burnt by an aircraft over given intervals of a flight, using open data sources, as a basis for estimating emissions. The challenge ran in two phases from 1 October to 30 November 2025. It attracted 179 teams from 48 countries; 53 of them submitted predictions, with 2,127 submissions in total.

**Winners** (ranked by RMSE on the held-out test set):

| Place | Team | RMSE | Members | Affiliation | Country | Code |
|-------|------|-----:|---------|-------------|:-------:|:----:|
| 1st | [resourceful-quiver](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/dc2025/teams/resourceful-quiver.html) | 200.83 | M.F. Rahman et al. | [TU Delft](https://www.tudelft.nl/) | NL | [{{< iconify fa6-brands github >}}](https://github.com/PRC-Data-Challenge-2025/resourceful-quiver) |
| 2nd | [jubilant-vase](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/dc2025/teams/jubilant-vase.html) | 211.99 | A. Vernin et al. | [Sapienza](https://www.uniroma1.it/) / [ENSAI](https://ensai.fr/) | FR | [{{< iconify fa6-brands github >}}](https://github.com/PRC-Data-Challenge-2025/jubilant-vase) |
| 3rd | [outspoken-tornado](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/dc2025/teams/outspoken-tornado.html) | 219.85 | B. Ryelandt et al. | [Euranova](https://euranova.eu/) | BE | [{{< iconify fa6-brands github >}}](https://github.com/PRC-Data-Challenge-2025/outspoken-tornado) |

### 2024 PRC Data Challenge — Actual Takeoff Weight Prediction

Participants predicted the actual takeoff weight (ATOW) of flights using open ADS-B trajectory data, weather information, and aircraft characteristics from a dataset of 369,013 European flights. The challenge attracted 132 teams, with around 550 submissions; 43 teams from 22 countries reached the final phase.

**Winners** (announced at the 12th OpenSky Symposium, Hamburg, November 2024):

| Place | Team | RMSE | Members | Affiliation | Country | Code |
|-------|------|-----:|---------|-------------|:-------:|:----:|
| 1st | [likable_jelly](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/dc2024/teams.html#team_likable_jelly) | 1561.63 kg | R. Alligier et al. | [ENAC](https://www.enac.fr/) | FR | [{{< iconify fa6-brands github >}}](https://github.com/PRC-Data-Challenge-2024/team_likable_jelly) |
| 2nd | [tiny_rainbow](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/dc2024/teams.html#team_tiny_rainbow) | 2217.75 kg | M. Murca et al. | [ITA](https://www.ita.br/) | BR | [{{< iconify fa6-brands github >}}](https://github.com/PRC-Data-Challenge-2024/team_tiny_rainbow) |
| 3rd | [brave_pillow](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/dc2024/teams.html#team_brave_pillow) | 2270.06 kg | A. Tassanbi et al. | [TU Delft](https://www.tudelft.nl/) | NL | [{{< iconify fa6-brands github >}}](https://github.com/PRC-Data-Challenge-2024/team_brave_pillow) |

## Get Involved

Interested in participating in a future PRC Data Challenge? Follow the [PRC Data Challenge page](https://ansperformance.eu/study/data-challenge/) for announcements, or contact us at [pru-support@eurocontrol.int](mailto:pru-support@eurocontrol.int).
